title: Re-lay a lay-in ceiling tile from below: turn it square on the tee tops and let it down onto the grid flanges
instruction: Put the ceiling tile back into its opening in the grid.
context: Lay-in tiles in suspended T-bar ceilings are lifted out and put back many times a week by the people who work above them: general maintenance and repair workers (about 1.5 million in the US), electricians (about 0.8 million) and HVAC, fire-alarm and low-voltage technicians open the ceiling on most service calls in offices, schools, shops and hospitals by pushing a tile up and leaving it lying askew across the tops of the tees. Re-laying it is done from below, hands up in the opening: the tile is turned back square on the narrow tee tops with the fingertips, centred (it has about 2 mm to spare between the tees' bulbs), let down 38 mm between the tee webs and set flat on 24 mm flanges that it overlaps by under 9 mm a side, without knocking the loose neighbouring tiles. A 0.6 m tile resting on four narrow steel edges only spins or tips under one hand, so it takes both.
setup: Bench top z = 0.7475 m; x forward from the arm bases, y to the left. A section of 15/16 in exposed-tee suspended-ceiling grid (24 in / 609.6 mm module, 2 rows x 3 columns of 2 ft x 2 ft bays, white steel tees 38 mm tall with 24 mm flanges, e.g. Armstrong Prelude XL) hangs on 12 ga wire from a 40 mm aluminium test frame (four posts at x 0.165 / 1.445, y +-0.944, 0.69 m tall), its flange face 462 mm above the bench. Tee centre lines: x = 0.195, 0.805, 1.415; y = -0.914, -0.305, 0.305, 0.914. The target bay is the middle bay of the near row, centre (0.50, 0.00), clear opening 585.6 mm square. The five other bays hold loose identical tiles resting on their flanges. Three 1-5/8 in steel strut channels cross the plenum at x = 0.30, 0.70, 1.11, their undersides 220 mm above the flange face. The work tile, a 2 ft x 2 ft square-edge lay-in mineral-fibre tile (603 x 603 x 16 mm, about 1.1 kg, e.g. Armstrong 1810 Cortega), lies askew on top of the grid over its own opening: centre (0.506, -0.004), turned 12 deg counter-clockwise seen from above, resting across the tops of the four surrounding tees (its underside 38 mm above the flange face). Arms start at rest below the ceiling.
scoring: From the six tiles' poses and the hands' TCPs. 0.1: turned to within 5 deg of square over the opening. 0.2: within 1 deg of square and its centre within 5 mm of the bay centre. 0.6: seated - all four bottom corners within 3 mm of the flange face, bearing at least 4 mm on all four flanges, at rest 1 s (a tile at rest in the opening but cocked on a flange scores 0.35 instead). Once seated: +0.04 per neighbouring tile never lifted more than 3 mm or shifted more than 5 mm (5 tiles, 0.2), and +0.2 when both hands are withdrawn (50 mm below the flange face or 50 mm clear of the tile) for 2 s with the tile still seated. Dropped (scores 0, latches): the tile lands on the bench, or is more than 150 mm below the flange face with no hand within 100 mm of it for 0.5 s; a tile carried down through the opening and brought back up (e.g. to put it in diagonally) is not dropped. Doing nothing scores 0. Real trial: the 0.1/0.2 milestones (tile still on top of the grid) are read from the video from below, against a tape line on the near tee and a pencil mark at the tile's centre: tile edge parallel to the tee within 5 deg / 1 deg, centre mark within 5 mm of the bay-centre mark on a cross-string; a straightedge or steel rule across the opening from below for flush within 3 mm on all four sides; tape marks on the neighbours' edges and the video for lift/shift, drops and the hands' withdrawal.
reset_notes: Fixed start, no randomisation. Reset: push the work tile up from below, turn it 12 deg counter-clockwise and lay it across the four tee tops with its corners on the tape marks on the neighbouring tiles (about 20 s); check the five neighbours sit flat on their flanges. Mineral-fibre tiles shed dust and their edges wear with handling: swap in a fresh work tile every 20 trials (or sooner if an edge is chipped), or use a vinyl-faced washable lay-in tile of the same size and weight class (e.g. Armstrong Clean Room VL, 24 x 24 x 5/8 in square lay-in), which does not shed and wipes clean.
fidelity: PhysX 240 Hz, all rigid. Grid is one fixed body of analytic box colliders per tee (24 x 2 mm flange, 2 mm web, 3 x 8 mm bulb); tiles are rigid 603 x 603 x 16 mm boxes (real tiles flex slightly, so are a little more forgiving). Friction: tile on painted steel 0.35, tile on gripper 0.75. Top camera sits just below the ceiling plane and sees it edge-on; the recorded overview camera looks up at the bay. Demo is closed loop on the tile's measured pose; nothing is moved by script.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 after 129 steps (6.45 simulated seconds); termination: DreamSessionExpired:expired. Scripted/teleoperated demo: 1 after 294 steps.
